CHAPTER II.
The Pool of Tears


"Curiouser and curiouser!" cried Alice, for she had grown to more
than nine feet high after eating the cake. She hurried to the garden
door with the golden key, but could only look through with one eye.
She sat down and cried, weeping gallons of tears that formed a great
pool around her.

The White Rabbit came trotting back, muttering about the Duchess,
and dropped a fan and a pair of white kid gloves when Alice spoke to
him. Fanning herself with the fan made her shrink again, so quickly
that she nearly disappeared, and then she fell into the very pool of
tears she had cried earlier, now swimming in salt water.

She met a Mouse swimming in the pool, and after some awkward
attempts at conversation about cats and dogs, they swam together to
the shore along with a growing crowd of birds and animals who had
also fallen into the pool.
